root_cause.text: The net/shaper netlink SET/DELETE/GROUP write path acquired only a netdev reference in the pre_doit stage and deferred taking the netdev instance lock until inside the handler, allowing netdev unregister/flush to race with net_shaper_hierarchy_setup() and create a hierarchy after flush.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says “The netdev may get unregistered in between the time we take the ref and the time we lock it. We may allocate the hierarchy after flush has already run, which would lead to a leak,” and the patch fixes this by adding net_shaper_ctx_setup_lock() using netdev_get_by_index_lock(), switching write ops to net_shaper_nl_pre_doit_write/post_doit_write, and removing per-handler late net_shaper_lock()/unlock() calls.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused net_shaper binding lock/unlock wrapper helpers to simplify the code.
intent_record.what: The change deletes two static helper functions, net_shaper_lock() and net_shaper_unlock(), which previously switched on binding->type and called netdev_lock(binding->netdev) and netdev_unlock(binding->netdev) for NET_SHAPER_BINDING_TYPE_NETDEV.
intent_record.how: At runtime this removes these wrapper functions from the file, eliminating the abstraction layer for locking and unlocking a net_shaper_binding; behavior only changes if callers are updated elsewhere to lock directly or no longer need these helpers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add locked netdev context setup and matching unlock cleanup for net shaper write handlers so operations run under the required device hierarchy lock.
intent_record.what: The change adds a new helper function, net_shaper_ctx_setup_lock(), that validates the required netlink attribute, looks up a network device by ifindex using netdev_get_by_index_lock(), verifies that the device has net_shaper_ops, stores the locked netdev in the context binding, and returns appropriate errors on failure. It also adds a matching cleanup helper, net_shaper_ctx_cleanup_unlock(), which unlocks the bound netdev when the context refers to a net device. Comments indicate this locked setup path is intended for write handlers and not dump handlers.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this introduces a context setup path for write operations that acquires the hierarchy-protecting device lock before operating on the netdev and provides a dedicated unlock cleanup path afterward. This prevents write handlers from accessing or modifying net shaper state without holding the required lock, while still rejecting missing attributes, nonexistent devices, and unsupported devices with explicit errors.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clarify the net_shaper_hierarchy_setup() locking comment to document the correct hierarchy-protecting lock context.
intent_record.what: The comment above net_shaper_hierarchy_setup() was changed from saying the function is called under "the net shaper lock" to saying it is called under "the lock protecting the hierarchy (instance lock for netdev)".
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior; it clarifies the locking requirement for callers by documenting the specific lock context that protects the hierarchy, especially for the netdev case.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add pre/post write doit handlers to set up locked net_shaper context before execution and cleanly unlock it afterward.
intent_record.what: Two new functions were added: net_shaper_nl_pre_doit_write(), which casts info->ctx to struct net_shaper_nl_ctx, verifies at build time that the context fits in info->ctx with BUILD_BUG_ON, and returns net_shaper_ctx_setup_lock(info, NET_SHAPER_A_IFINDEX, ctx); and net_shaper_nl_post_doit_write(), which calls net_shaper_ctx_cleanup_unlock() on the cast info->ctx.
intent_record.how: This introduces dedicated pre/post handlers for write doit netlink operations that initialize per-request context and acquire the appropriate lock before execution, then release and clean up that context afterward. At runtime, write operations using these hooks will execute under proper locking and context management, preventing unsafe concurrent access and ensuring cleanup after the operation completes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor net_shaper_nl_set_doit() to use direct returns and remove local binding lock/unlock handling while preserving its success and error behavior.
intent_record.what: The function net_shaper_nl_set_doit() was changed to remove the initial net_shaper_lock(binding) call, remove the unlock label and final net_shaper_unlock(binding) call, replace several 'ret = ...; goto unlock;' error paths with immediate 'return' statements, simplify some braced single-statement conditionals, and return 0 directly after net_shaper_commit() instead of returning ret.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now exits immediately on parse, allocation, lookup, pre-insert, or set-operation failures without taking or releasing the binding lock in this function, and it explicitly returns success after commit. This shifts locking responsibility out of this function and avoids performing an unlock here, while preserving the same error codes for the failure cases.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify net_shaper_nl_delete_doit() by removing local lock/unlock handling and converting goto-based error paths into direct returns.
intent_record.what: The function net_shaper_nl_delete_doit() was changed to remove the explicit net_shaper_lock(binding) and net_shaper_unlock(binding) calls, replace several 'ret = ...; goto unlock;' error paths with direct early returns, simplify the hierarchy and shaper existence checks into single-line returns of -ENOENT, and return the result of __net_shaper_delete(binding, shaper, info->extack) directly instead of assigning it to ret and falling through an unlock label.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the delete handler no longer acquires and releases the binding lock in this function and instead exits immediately on parse, lookup, or pre-delete failures. This changes locking behavior by avoiding the previous local lock scope, likely relying on locking being handled elsewhere or by lower-level code, while preserving the same visible error codes and delete operation flow.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid taking the net shaper lock before input validation and memory allocation by returning early on invalid leaves or allocation failure.
intent_record.what: The change removes the early call to net_shaper_lock(binding) before validating NET_SHAPER_A_LEAVES and allocating the leaves array, and replaces the error paths for zero leaves_count and failed kcalloc() from setting ret and jumping to an unlock label with direct returns of -EINVAL and -ENOMEM.
intent_record.how: This makes the function exit immediately on invalid input or allocation failure before acquiring the lock, avoiding unnecessary locking and preventing execution from following an unlock-based error path when no lock has been taken in these cases.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an incorrect unlock from the `free_leaves` return path in `net_shaper_nl_group_doit()` to fix cleanup behavior.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the `unlock:` label and deletes the `net_shaper_unlock(binding);` call that was immediately before the function's `return ret;` in `net_shaper_nl_group_doit()`, leaving the `free_leaves:` label to fall through directly to the return.
intent_record.how: At runtime, execution reaching the `free_leaves:` path no longer performs `net_shaper_unlock(binding)` before returning, which changes cleanup behavior by avoiding that unlock operation on this error/exit path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unnecessary outer binding locking from net_shaper_flush() so cleanup uses only the xarray lock and avoids nested locking issues.
intent_record.what: The change removes the calls to net_shaper_lock(binding) before iterating over hierarchy->shapers and net_shaper_unlock(binding) after the xarray traversal and cleanup in net_shaper_flush(), leaving only xa_lock(&hierarchy->shapers) and xa_unlock(&hierarchy->shapers) around the erase-and-free loop.
intent_record.how: At runtime, net_shaper_flush() no longer acquires the outer binding lock while flushing the shapers xarray, relying solely on the xarray's own lock for synchronization during element removal and freeing. This changes lock behavior by eliminating nested locking around this cleanup path, which can avoid unnecessary locking and potential lock ordering or deadlock issues while preserving protection of the xarray contents.

intent_record.what: The NET_SHAPER_CMD_SET, NET_SHAPER_CMD_DELETE, and NET_SHAPER_CMD_GROUP entries in the net_shaper_nl_ops array were updated to replace .pre_doit = net_shaper_nl_pre_doit with .pre_doit = net_shaper_nl_pre_doit_write, and .post_doit = net_shaper_nl_post_doit with .post_doit = net_shaper_nl_post_doit_write.
intent_record.how: These three netlink commands will now execute the write-specific pre_doit and post_doit handlers instead of the generic ones, changing the runtime setup and teardown behavior for modifying operations so they use write-path handling appropriate for state-changing requests.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add exported pre/post doit callback prototypes for net_shaper write operations so write requests can use dedicated generic netlink hooks.
intent_record.what: The header adds declarations for two new functions: net_shaper_nl_pre_doit_write(const struct genl_split_ops *ops, struct sk_buff *skb, struct genl_info *info) and net_shaper_nl_post_doit_write(const struct genl_split_ops *ops, struct sk_buff *skb, struct genl_info *info), alongside the existing pre/post doit callback prototypes.
intent_record.how: This exposes separate pre- and post-doit callback entry points for write operations, allowing runtime code to distinguish write handling from the existing generic and capability-related doit hooks when these functions are implemented and used.

candidates.rationale: SET used the generic pre_doit handler that only acquired a netdev reference rather than the write-side locked context, enabling the race with unregister/flush described in the root cause.
DELETE likewise used the non-write pre_doit path, so it did not establish the required netdev instance lock before entering the mutating handler.
GROUP also used the generic pre_doit callback instead of the write-specific one, leaving write operations exposed to racing device teardown/flush.

This cleanup shows the pre-fix context lifetime management only held a netdev reference; the root cause is precisely that reference-taking occurred without also holding the required device lock across write operations.

vuln_statements.explanation: The SET/DELETE/GROUP mutating netlink operations were wired to the generic pre_doit handler, which only acquired a netdev reference and did not take the write-side netdev instance lock before entering the handler. This directly matches the root cause: unregister/flush could race with net_shaper_hierarchy_setup() and allow hierarchy creation after flush.

This statement reflects the pre-fix lifetime model in which the write path context only managed a netdev reference. The fix rationale indicates the bug was that write operations relied on reference-based context setup/teardown instead of holding the required device lock across the operation, enabling the teardown/flush race.

bic_trace_step.reason: The root cause is specific to the netlink SET/DELETE/GROUP write path: pre_doit only takes a netdev reference, and the instance lock is deferred until inside the handler, allowing unregister/flush to race with hierarchy setup. In this commit, the shown function bodies for the write handlers do not implement any write-path logic at all: `int net_shaper_nl_set_doit(...) { return -EOPNOTSUPP; }` and `int net_shaper_nl_delete_doit(...) { return -EOPNOTSUPP; }`. There is also no GROUP handler implementation shown. The pre-handler `net_shaper_nl_pre_doit()` does indeed only call `net_shaper_generic_pre(info, NET_SHAPER_A_IFINDEX)`, and `net_shaper_ctx_setup()` only acquires a netdev reference via `netdev_get_by_index(...)`, with no instance lock taken there. However, because the vulnerable construct requires an actual write path that later performs hierarchy creation/modification after this pre-stage, and that write logic is absent in this commit, the vulnerable write-path construct is not present here. Likewise, the fix is not present either: there is no evidence of taking the netdev instance lock in pre_doit or otherwise hardening SET/DELETE/GROUP against flush/unregister races. So the code is sufficient to determine that this commit does not yet contain the vulnerable write-path implementation, and also does not yet contain the later fix.
